The file must define the function: ```python def policy(you, opponent) -> str: ... ``` You are always the player to move. State representation: * The board is 6x6. * You are given two 6x6 arrays (or array-like objects) containing only 0/1 integers: * `you[r][c] == 1` means your marble is at row r, col c * `opponent[r][c] == 1` means the opponent marble is at row r, col c * Empty cell means `you[r][c] == 0` and `opponent[r][c] == 0` * You may assume positions are valid (no overlaps), i.e. never `you[r][c] == opponent[r][c] == 1`. Move format: A move is a single string formatted exactly as: ```text "row,col,quad,dir" ``` Where: * `row` is 1..6 (1-indexed) * `col` is 1..6 (1-indexed) * `quad` is 0..3 * `dir` is `L` or `R` (Left/Anticlockwise or Right/Clockwise) Example (this is only an example of the action syntax): * `"6,5,2,L"` means place at row 6 col 5, then rotate quadrant 2 left. Rules (Pentago): 1. On your turn you must output a legal move string: (a) Place exactly one of your marbles on an empty cell (row 1..6, col 1..6), then (b) Rotate exactly one quadrant (quad 0..3) 90 degrees in the chosen direction (L or R). 2. Quadrants are the 3x3 sub-boards, indexed as follows: * `quad = 0`: rows 1..3, cols 1..3 (top-left) * `quad = 1`: rows 1..3, cols 4..6 (top-right) * `quad = 2`: rows 4..6, cols 1..3 (bottom-left) * `quad = 3`: rows 4..6, cols 4..6 (bottom-right) 3. Rotation rotates the chosen 3x3 sub-board in place, affecting BOTH players' marbles in that quadrant. * `L` is 90 degrees anticlockwise. * `R` is 90 degrees clockwise. 4. Win condition: * After the placement and rotation are applied, a player wins if they have 5 (or more) marbles in a row in any straight line: horizontal, vertical, or diagonal (either diagonal direction). 5. If both players have a 5-in-a-row after your move is applied, the result is a draw. If neither player has a 5-in-a-row and the board is full, the result is a draw. Policy requirements: * Implement `policy(you, opponent)` to always return a legal move string. * A legal move must: - Choose an empty cell for the placement. - Specify `quad` in 0..3. - Specify `dir` in {`L`, `R`}. * You should assume `policy` is never called when there is no legal move (i.e., at least one empty cell exists). * You must ALWAYS return a legal move string. It is EXTREMELY IMPORTANT that you ALWAYS return a legal move string. You will be disqualified if you do not return a legal move string. You may use any standard Python imports, including numpy. Your code is allowed 1 second of execution time on a modern 3GHz CPU. Output your thinking before the code. Output the Python source code for your policy surrounded by ... tags.
